clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10285 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end; the board reported on September 19, 1951 (held report), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10285 at 16 FR 9135, in the Federal Register of September 8, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10285 and is signed September 6, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between The Denver & Rio Grande Western Railroad Company, including the Denver & Salt Lake Railroad Company, a carrier under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of the carrier's transportation system. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: "Nothing in this order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under the said Executive Order No. 10155."; a sentence directing the board to "report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order" (the text layer drops the sentence's first word); and "In performing its functions under this order the Board shall comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended." Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10285 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10285_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10285_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ec5eddd465.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created September 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10285, and its title page and letter of transmittal are dated at Denver, September 19, 1951. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10285, 10286 and 10287) and the front matter of the board's report.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause, and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right; a bounded search of the held Executive Order 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR disposition notes shows no residual effect.
